title: Nightwatch incident curation — 02 Apr 2026
content:
Summary:

Short summary: Night shift observed a region-localized latency surge affecting hosted-api-route /v1/generate in us-west-2 between 2026-04-02T01:12Z and 2026-04-02T02:04Z. Root symptom: increased p95 token generation latency (200ms->1.1s) and a ~12% error bump (502/504) tied to a temporary memcached KV cache thrash on dedicated provisioned nodes. Impact scope: ~6% of active requests during peak minute; only hosted customers on model variant rwd-7b-q4 experienced degraded tail latencies.

What alerted us:
- Pager alert: p95-gen-latency-us-west-2 crossed 800ms (pager page) at 01:12Z (INC-4521 triggered).
- Dashboards: cost/latency anomaly filter flagged CPU saturation on pool-dedicated-gpu-3 at 01:18Z.
- Synthetic monitors (canary prompts) showed timeouts starting 01:10Z.

Timeline (UTC):
- 01:10 — Canary failures begin, first user-reported Slack thread in #hosted-api.
- 01:12 — Pager fired for p95-gen-latency-us-west-2. I (Maya) ACK'd and started bridge.
- 01:15 — Quick triage: model variants pinned to ded-3 pool; observed elevated KV miss rate on memcached cluster node mcd-usw2-07.
- 01:22 — SRE runbook step: failover memcached replica attempted (manual script run, see commands below). Failover succeeded but thrash continued.
- 01:28 — Observed a thundering herd: multiple hosts re-populating cache with large prefixes (batch jobs from a customer triggered TTL churn).
- 01:35 — Eng infra (Arjun) rolled a temporary rate-limit policy for the offending customer route on the edge (edge-ratelimit-sim) to reduce cache churn.
- 01:46 — Errors reduced, latencies started trending down.
- 02:04 — p95 returned to baseline for rwd-7b-q4; incident declared mitigated and moved to post-incident analysis.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Manual memcached failover of mcd-usw2-07 -> mcd-usw2-09 (script: infra/tools/memcfailover.sh --from 07 --to 09).
- Edge-side per-cust route throttling (APPLIED: cust-8452: 50 rps burst cap) to slow the namespace rehydration.
- Temporarily pinned fallback model variant rwd-7b-q4->rwd-7b-q4-lite for a subset of requests to reduce memory pressure.

Customer impact / comms:
- Affected customers: internal alert shows customer cust-8452 heavy batch job; no enterprise SLA claim yet.
- Outreach: Lina opened a ticket with customer success to coordinate (INC-4521 -> CS-6789). Draft note attached in linked artifacts.

Runbook notes / gaps found:
- Runbook "kv-cache-evictions" (Confluence) covers TTL churn but lacks a quick CLI checklist for applying per-customer edge throttles.
- Failover steps assume a healthy replication lag; in this case replication lag was ~12s which contributed to brief cache inconsistency and rehydration storm. Need to add a check for replication-lag <5s before automatic failovers.
- No automated detection for large prefix re-population; we should add an alert on sustained cache fill rates (keys/sec) + top keyspace pollers.

Follow-ups / action items (owners & deadlines):
- Add replication-lag precondition to memcached failover script (Arjun) — due 2026-04-07.
- Create an edge-runbook snippet for per-customer soft throttles and link to runbooks (Maya) — due 2026-04-06.
- Implement a cache-fill-rate alert dashboard (SRE-317) and add top-keyspace sampling tool to infra toolbox (Oliver) — due 2026-04-14.
- CS outreach: coordinate next steps with cust-8452 about batch jobs and recommend staggered windows (Lina) — update ticket by 2026-04-03 EOD.
- Postmortem doc draft (inc-4521-postmortem) — I will start draft; request reviewers Arjun, Lina, Oliver — draft ready by 2026-04-05.

Commands run (notes to self):
- infra/tools/memcfailover.sh --from mcd-usw2-07 --to mcd-usw2-09  # manual failover; watched replication status
- infra/edgectl set-rate-limit --customer cust-8452 --route /v1/generate --rps 50 --burst 100 --reason "mitigate cache rehydration"
- monitoring/queries/top-cache-fillers --region us-west-2 --minutes 30  # used to identify offending keys

Quick debugging snippets (for next shift):
- Check memcached replication lag: redis-cli -h mcd-usw2-07 info replication | grep lag
- Top keyspace poll: monitoring/queries/top-cache-fillers --region us-west-2 --limit 20
- If memcached node consistently >85% evictions, consider temporary increase to cache size on spare node or soft throttle per-customer.

What I learned / notes to retain:
- Large customer batch operations that repopulate prefixes can look like DoS from the cache layer — visible on host CPU and KV miss rate before requests fail.
- Edge throttles are a quick, effective mitigation and should be part of the runbook with example commands.
- Automated failovers are risky without a replication-lag guard; they can increase short-term inconsistency.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Did the customer's batch job spike because of an upstream retry loop? Lina to investigate with CS and product.
- Should we proactively notify high-throughput customers about guidelines to avoid TTL churn? Product & CS discussion needed.

Next shift handoff (to nightbridge on 2026-04-03):
- Primary: Oliver Reed (oliver) — follow up on SRE-317; verify cache-fill-rate alert is in preview.
- Secondary: Arjun Patel — finish the replication-lag precondition change and sanity-check memcached replication metrics.
- Please review draft postmortem (linked artifact) and add any missing timeline items.

Misc / scratch notes:
- Revisit memcached sizing doc: sizing-guides/cache-sizing-2025 (may need minor updates).
- Note to self: add sample edgectl commands to runbook + small cookbook for "soft throttle" vs "hard throttle" decisions.

End of log.

-- Maya
